note: Part 1 of 2: authored items for the sparse Python-Core chapters s12 (Dictionaries), s13 (OOP), s14 (Functions), s15 (Exceptions/Files/Modules), s16 (Advanced Python). Part 2 (s01-s11) is python-core-foundations.json.

items.q: dict lookup average O(1) kyun hota hai, list ki tarah scan kyun nahi karta?
items.a: Key ka hash nikalkar us bucket me direct jump karta hai (hash table), isliye list jaisa linear scan nahi lagta. Worst case (sab hash collide) O(n) ho jaata hai, par average O(1) rehta hai.

items.q: Membership check ke liye dict ya set list se better kab hota hai?
items.a: Jab baar-baar membership ya key lookup karna ho: dict/set average O(1), list O(n). Agar order chahiye bhi ho aur lookup zyada, to dict (3.7+ me insertion order preserved) sahi choice hai.

items.q: Python 3.7 se dict insertion order guarantee karta hai — practical fayda kya hai?
items.a: Output/JSON ka order deterministic hota hai, isliye tests stable rehte hain aur config ki key order maintain hoti hai. Pehle OrderedDict ki zarurat padti thi, ab plain dict kaafi hai.

items.q: 'Key must be hashable' ka matlab kya hai?
items.a: Key ke liye __hash__ aur __eq__ consistent hone chahiye — yani immutable values (str, int, tuple) keys ban sakti hain, mutable (list, set, dict) nahi, kyunki badalne par hash badal jaata aur lookup toot jaata.
items.x: Immutable hi key ban sakti hai.

items.q: Interview: 'word frequency kaise count karoge?' — idiomatic Python jawab kya hai?
items.a: collections.Counter(words) — agar manual likhna ho to counts = {}; for w in words: counts[w] = counts.get(w, 0) + 1; aur top-N ke liye Counter.most_common(n) use karo.

items.q: d[key] aur d.get(key, default) me production code me kaunsa choose karoge?
items.a: Agar key ka hona contract hai to d[key] use karo (fail fast, KeyError trace deta hai). Optional key ke liye d.get(key, default). Silent .get() se missing-config bugs chhup jaate hain.

items.q: Multiple config dicts ko precedence ke saath merge karne ka pattern kya hai?
items.a: Order me update karo: merged = {}; merged.update(defaults); merged.update(env); merged.update(cli_overrides) — baad wala jeetta hai. Nested ke liye recursive merge likhna padta hai.

items.q: List dict ki key kyun nahi ban sakti — interview me technically kaise explain karoge?
items.a: list unhashable hai (mutable), isliye uska hash stable nahi ho sakta; dict lookup hash par chalta hai. Tuple of hashable items ya frozenset use karo agar composite key chahiye.

items.q: Ek text ka word frequency dict banao (case-insensitive, punctuation ignore) aur top 3 words return karo.
Dict ko invert karo (values → keys) aur duplicate values ko list me rakho.
items.x: setdefault se naya list banta hai, phir append.

items.q: Do dicts merge karo aur same key ke numeric values jod do.
items.x: get(k, 0) se missing key ka dard khatam.

items.q: Nested dict se safe deep-get likho: get_deep(d, ['a','b','c'], default=None).
items.x: Har step par type + key check.

items.q: d = {1: 'a', True: 'b'}; print(d) — output kya aur kyun?
items.a: {1: 'b'} — Python me True == 1 aur hash(True) == hash(1), isliye dono ek hi key maani jaati hain aur baad wali value overwrite kar deti hai.

items.q: d = {}; d['self'] = d; print(d) — kya print hoga?
items.a: {'self': {...}} — dict khud ko reference karta hai, isliye repr cycle ko {...} se dikhata hai (infinite print nahi hota). JSON serialize karne par yahi cycle RecursionError deti hai.

items.q: print({'a': 1}.get('b')) aur print({'a': 1}.get('b', 0)) ke output batao.
items.a: Pehla None, doosra 0. Default na dene par method None return karta hai — isliye .get() ka result directly compare karne me None-vs-missing ka farq chhup sakta hai.

items.q: Loop ke andar dict se item delete karo to kya hota hai?
items.a: RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration. Fix: list(d) ya list(d.items()) par iterate karo, phir delete; ya comprehension se naya dict banao.

items.q: Config loader random KeyError deta hai jab optional field missing hoti hai. Fix?
items.a: Optional key ke liye d.get(key, default) use karo, ya schema/defaults dict define karke usse seed karo; required key ke liye fail fast rakho aur error message me key ka naam + config source do.

items.q: d.items()[0] TypeError deta hai. Sahi tarika?
items.a: items() ek view hai, indexable nahi. Fix: list(d.items())[0], ya next(iter(d.items())) — aur agar order matter karta hai to insertion order par bharosa karke hi index chuno.
items.x: View ko list me convert karo.

items.q: sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r['score']) kabhi KeyError de raha hai. Root cause aur robust fix?
items.a: Kuch rows me 'score' key hi nahi hai. Fix: r.get('score', 0) use karo, ya pehle data validate karo (schema check) taaki missing field input par hi pakdi jaaye — silent default metric badal sakta hai.
items.x: Missing key ko explicitly handle karo.

items.q: {'a': 1, 'b': 2} == {'b': 2, 'a': 1} — True ya False? Aur is se tests kyun rukte hain?
items.a: True — dict equality ka key order se koi lena-dena nahi. Tests tab flaky hote hain jab tum str(d) ya JSON string compare karte ho; isliye string compare ke bajaye dict compare karo.

items.q: Real-world: inventory merge — do warehouses ka stock dict merge karo, report me total aur sirf-positive items dikhao.
items.x: defaultdict se accumulate karo, phir filter.

items.q: Real-world: records ko field ke hisaab se group karo (mini group-by) — orders ko customer_id par.
Real-world: config layering — defaults, env vars aur CLI args ko precedence ke saath ek dict me banao.
items.a:
def load_config(defaults, env, cli):
    cfg = dict(defaults)
    cfg.update({k: v for k, v in env.items() if v is not None})
    cfg.update({k: v for k, v in cli.items() if v is not None})
    # validate required keys early, fail fast with the key name
    return cfg
items.x: None mean 'not set', isliye skip karo.

items.q: Real-world: dict cache jo max size ke baad purani entries nikaal de (simple LRU).
Checkpoint: dict ke paanch commonly used methods likho aur ek-ek ka kaam.
items.a: get (default ke saath lookup), setdefault (na ho to set karke do), items (k,v pairs), keys/values (views), pop (nikalo aur return).

items.q: Checkpoint: dict comprehension ka syntax aur ek example likho.
items.a: {k: v for k, v in pairs if condition} — jaise {w: len(w) for w in words}.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumne is index/search ke liye dict kyun chuni, list of tuples kyun nahi?'
items.a: Lookup path O(1) chahiye tha (per query kaam hota hai) aur keys unique hain, isliye dict ka natural fit tha. List of tuples rakhta to har lookup O(n) scan hota, aur values ki uniqueness bhi manually enforce karni padti.
items.x: Data shape + complexity se justify karo.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare dict-based cache me memory kab problem banegi aur tum kya karoge?'
items.a: Jab entry count days tak badhta rahe aur values badi hon — memory unbounded grow karti hai aur process restart par sab lost. Plan: max size + LRU eviction, key ko normalize karke duplicate reduce, aur metrics me cache size/hit-rate expose karna.

items.q: Class attribute aur instance attribute me farq kya hai?
items.a: Class attribute class par define hota hai aur sab instances share karte hain; instance attribute self.x se banake per-object state rakhta hai. Immutable defaults ke liye class attribute theek hai, mutable (list) ko instance me banao.

items.q: self ka asli kaam kya hai?
items.a: self instance ka pehla argument hai jo method call par automatically pass hota hai — isse method ko pata chalta hai kis object par kaam karna hai. Ye Python ka explicit 'this' hai, syntax sugar nahi.

items.q: __init__ aur __new__ me farq batao.
items.a: __new__ object banata hai (instance creation), __init__ us bane hue object ko initialize karta hai. Normal code me __init__ hi likhte hain; __new__ tab chahiye jab immutable types subclass kar rahe ho ya custom instance banani ho.
items.x: Banane ke liye new, set karne ke liye init.

items.q: Multiple inheritance me method resolution Python me kaise hoti hai?
items.a: MRO (C3 linearization) left-to-right, depth-first with dedupe — ClassName.__mro__ se exact order dikhta hai. super() MRO ke hisaab se agla class call karta hai, isliye cooperative sharing possible hoti hai.

items.q: Python me encapsulation kaise karte hain (private/protected jaisa byte)?
items.a: Convention se: _protected (team ke liye), __private (name mangling se accidental override se bachaata hai, sach me private nahi hai). Enforcement runtime par nahi hoti — isliye tests/review se hi discipline aati hai.

items.q: 'Composition over inheritance' — iska practical matlab kya hai?
items.a: Inheritance tab jab 'is-a' relation ho aur behaviour genuinely share ho. Jab sirf code reuse chahiye ya 'has-a' relation ho, to object ko parameter/injection ke roop me use karo — warna deep hierarchy har badlaav par phail jaati hai.

items.q: __str__ aur __repr__ me interview me kaise farq bataoge?
items.a: __repr__ developer ke liye unambiguous debug representation hai (lists/dicts me dikhta hai), __str__ user ke liye readable text. Best practice: __repr__ hamesha do, aur wahi __str__ ka default banao (__str__ = __repr__).

items.q: Ek dataclass banao Student(name, marks=0) aur uska readable repr dikhao.
Property se validated setter likho: price 0 se chhota ho to ValueError.
items.x: Property invariant ko ek jagah rakhta hai.

items.q: classmethod factory likho jo CSV row tuple se object banaye.
__eq__ aur __hash__ ko consistent banao (value object).
items.x: Equal objects ka hash bhi equal hona chahiye.

items.q: def f(items=[]): items.append(1); return items — f() do baar chalane par output?
items.a: Pehli call [1], doosri [1, 1] — default argument function definition ke time ek hi baar banta hai, isliye woh list calls ke beech share hoti hai. Fix: default None rakho aur andar naya list banao.
items.x: Default ek baar evaluate hota hai.

items.q: class A: tags = [] — do instances me tags.append karo, kya hoga?
items.a: Class-level mutable attribute share hota hai, isliye ek instance ka append doosre me bhi dikhega. Agar per-instance chahiye to __init__ me self.tags = [] karo.

items.q: isinstance(True, int) aur type(True) == int — output batao.
items.a: isinstance(True, int) True hai (bool int ka subclass hai), par type(True) == int False hai. Isliye validation me isinstance use karo, exact type compare nahi.

items.q: Instance method error deta hai: TypeError: show() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given. Fix?
items.a: Method ki definition me self bhoola gaya hai: def show(self):. Python instance ko pehla positional argument bhejta hai, isliye signature me self chahiye (staticmethod hota to @staticmethod lagta).
items.x: self bhoolna sabse common OOP bug.

items.q: Child class ke __init__ me parent ke attributes missing hain. Wajah aur fix?
items.a: Child ne __init__ override kiya par super().__init__(...) call nahi kiya, isliye parent ka initialization chhoot gaya. Fix: pehli line me super().__init__(...) aur parent ke required args pass karo.

items.q: Ek mutable default wala cache bug production me data leak kar raha hai (results calls ke beech mix ho rahe hain). Fix?
items.a: Signature me default [] / {} tha, isliye wahi object sab calls me share ho raha tha. Fix: default None + andar create karo (hat=None → hat = {} if hat is None else hat), aur ek test jo do calls ko isolate kare.
items.x: Isolation test ke saath fix karo.

items.q: Real-world: bank account class banao jisme withdraw overdraft rok de aur har change ka record rahe.
items.x: Invariant class ke andar enforce karo.

items.q: Real-world: plugin registry banao jahan registrations duplicate naam par fail karein.
Real-world: payment strategies (card/UPI/netbanking) ko ABC + strategy pattern se design karo.
items.x: Abstract base se interface lock hota hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: OOP ke chaar pillars aur Python me har ek ka ek tool likho.
items.a: Encapsulation (property/_private), Abstraction (ABC/abstractmethod), Inheritance (class Child(Parent), super()), Polymorphism (method override/duck typing).

items.q: Checkpoint: paanch common dunder methods aur unka kaam likho.
items.a: __init__ (setup), __repr__/__str__ (display), __eq__ (comparison), __hash__ (dict/set key), __len__/__iter__ (container behaviour).

items.q: Checkpoint: inheritance ke teen rules likho jo bugs rokte hain.
items.a: 1) Child __init__ me super().__init__() call karo. 2) Mutable defaults class level par na rakho. 3) Deep hierarchy ke bajaye composition socho.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumne ek god-class ko kaise toda (ya kaise todoge)?'
items.a: Behaviour ke hisaab se todta hoon, layer ke hisaab se nahi: data access, business rules aur formatting alag classes me, phir god-class sirf orchestrate karti hai. Har step par tests green rakhta hoon taaki refactor safe rahe.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhari classes ko kaise test karte ho — internals test karte ho ya behaviour?'
items.a: Public behaviour par tests likhta hoon (input → observable output/exception), internals mock nahi karta. Dependencies constructor me inject hoti hain, isliye tests me fake pass kar sakta hoon bina monkeypatching.

items.q: Project defense: 'Interviewer poochta hai tumne inheritance kahan use ki aur kyun' — jawab kya hoga?
items.a: Jahan sach me 'is-a' relation tha aur shared protocol chahiye tha: payment strategies ka common ABC, aur exception hierarchy. Reuse ke liye inheritance nahi ki — wahan composition use kiya, kyunki reuse ke liye hierarchy sabse mehnga tool hai.
items.x: Is-a ke liye haan, reuse ke liye nahi.

items.q: *args aur **kwargs kya karte hain aur signature me order kya hota hai?
items.a: *args extra positional arguments ko tuple me, **kwargs extra keyword arguments ko dict me collect karta hai. Order: positional, *args, keyword-only, **kwargs — yahi wrapper functions ka base hai.

items.q: Default argument kab evaluate hota hai aur uska practical consequence kya hai?
items.a: Function definition ke time (ek hi baar), call par nahi. Isliye mutable default (list/dict) calls ke beech share hota hai — None default + andar create karna safe pattern hai.

items.q: LEGB rule kya hai aur closure kaise banta hai?
items.a: Name lookup order: Local → Enclosing → Global → Builtins. Closure tab banta hai jab inner function outer function ke variable ko capture karta hai aur outer return hone ke baad bhi woh value jeeti rehti hai.

items.q: Bina return wala function kya return karta hai, aur isse kaunsa bug aata hai?
items.a: None return karta hai. Bug tab aata hai jab tum result ko number/list maan lete ho — None + 1 TypeError dega; isliye jaan-boojh kar None return karo ya explicitly return value do.

items.q: Mutable default argument ka classic bug interview me kaise explain karoge?
items.a: Default definition-time par banta hai, isliye wahi object har call me reuse hota hai aur state leak karta hai. Fix: default None rakho aur function ke andar fresh container banao; aur test jo do calls ko isolate kare.

items.q: lambda aur def me kab kaunsa choose karte ho?
items.a: lambda sirf single-expression, throwaway key/function ke liye (sorted key, map). Naam, docstring, multi-line logic, ya traceback readability chahiye to def — lambda stack trace me bekaar dikhta hai.

items.q: Pure function kya hai aur testing me kyun helpful hai?
items.a: Same input par same output, koi side effect nahi (I/O, global mutation nahi). Isliye test simple hota hai (koi mock nahi) aur refactor safe — side effects ko boundary par push karo.

items.q: Decorator likho jo function ke calls count kare aur woh count attribute me rakhe (functools.wraps ke saath).
items.x: wraps metadata bachata hai, counter attribute par jata hai.

items.q: Validation decorator likho jo non-negative int enforce kare.
Memoization decorator likho jo same args par dobara compute na kare.
items.x: Args key chahiye, isliye unhashable args avoid karo.

items.q: fns = [lambda: i for i in range(3)]; print([f() for f in fns]) — output?
items.a: [2, 2, 2] — closures variable ko late bind karte hain, isliye sab last value dekhte hain. Fix: default argument se bind karo: [lambda i=i: i for i in range(3)].

items.q: def f(x, acc=[]): acc.append(x); return acc → f(1) phir f(2) ka output?
items.a: f(1) → [1], f(2) → [1, 2]. Default list definition time par ek hi object hai, isliye calls ke beech share hoti hai (same mutable-default trap, function version).

items.q: Ye function UnboundLocalError deta hai: def f(): print(x); x = 1 → wajah?
items.a: Assignment hone se x poore function me local maana jaata hai, isliye print se pehle x unbound hai. print global value dikhani ho to global declare karo ya function param banao — global mutation se better param hai.

items.q: Decorator lagane ke baad function ka naam __main__.wrapper ho gaya aur docstring gayab. Fix?
items.a: functools.wraps(fn) laga do wrapper par — isse __name__, __doc__ aur metadata copy ho jaate hain (original function wrapper.__wrapped__ me milta hai).

items.q: Function galat values return kar raha hai kyunki ek branch me return missing hai. Robust fix kaise karoge?
items.a: Har branch me explicit return likho aur default path par error raise karo (ya typing se None return annotate karo). Test me woh branch specifically cover karo — silent None control-flow bug ka sabse aam source hai.

items.q: Code me list = [...] likha aur baad me list(...) call kar raha hai — kya galat aur fix?
items.a: Builtin list ko shadow kar diya, isliye builtin constructor unavailable ho gaya. Fix: variable ka naam badlo (items), aur lint (flake8 A001/B006 family) use karo taaki shadowing pakdi jaaye.

items.q: Real-world: flaky network call ke liye retry decorator likho (bounded attempts + backoff).
items.x: Configurable decorator + last attempt par raise.

items.q: Real-world: partial application se ek general function ko fixed-config version me convert karo.
items.a:
from functools import partial

def fetch(url, timeout=5, retries=2):
    return f'{url} timeout={timeout} retries={retries}'

fetch_fast = partial(fetch, timeout=1, retries=0)
print(fetch_fast('https://x'))
items.x: partial se pre-configured variant banta hai.

items.q: Real-world: SQL-ish filter DSL banao jo conditions ko composable functions se banaye.
Checkpoint: LEGB expand karo aur ek example do jahan E matter karta hai.
items.a: Local → Enclosing → Global → Builtins. Enclosing tab matter karta hai jab inner function outer ke variable ko padhe (closure) — jaise counter factory.

items.q: Checkpoint: * aur ** ka unpacking kaam likho (call ke waqt).
items.a: f(*items) → list/tuple ko positional args me unpack; f(**mapping) → dict ko keyword args me unpack (keys strings hone chahiye).
items.x: Unpacking dono direction me chalti hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: closure ke teen practical use-case likho.
items.a: Counter/factory functions, decorators (config capture), aur memoization/partial configuration.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare project me decorators kahan use kiye aur kya fayda mila?'
items.a: Timing/logging aur retry decorators: call sites saaf rehte hain aur cross-cutting concern ek jagah hota hai. Saath me functools.wraps aur explicit error handling rakha, taaki stack traces readable rahein.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumne typing hints use kiye ya nahi — kyun?'
items.a: Public functions aur data structures par haan (mypy jaisa mental check + editor support), kyunki isse interface contracts clear hote hain aur refactor safe hota hai. Internal one-liners par nahi, kyunki wahan noise zyada hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Ek 200-line function ko tumne kaise refactor kiya?'
items.a: Behaviour ke steps identify kiye (validate → transform → persist → report), har step ko named function banaya with tests, aur orchestration sabse upar rakha. Refactor ke baad line count kam nahi bhi hua, testability aur bug isolation bahut better hua.
items.x: Steps nikaalo, naam do, test karo.

items.q: try/except/else/finally — chaaron blocks kab chalte hain?
items.a: try: risky code. except: matching exception par. else: try successfully khatam hote hi (exception ke bina). finally: har case me (return/raise ke baad bhi) — cleanup ke liye.

items.q: Custom exception hierarchy ka fayda kya hai?
items.a: Caller specific errors ko catch kar sakta hai aur base class se sab ko ek jagah handle kar sakta hai (jaise AppError → ValidationError/NotFoundError). Isse API layer status codes ko cleanly map kar sakti hai.

items.q: Context manager ('with') andar se kaise kaam karta hai?
items.a: Object __enter__ (resource return karta hai) aur __exit__ (cleanup, exception pass hoti hai) implement karta hai; with block exit par __exit__ call hota hai, error aane par bhi. contextlib.contextmanager se generator wala short version milta hai.

items.q: import module aur from module import name me farq kya hai?
items.a: import module poora module object laata hai (module.name se access), from-import sirf naam bind karta hai — jo local namespace me shadow ya circular import ka risk badhata hai. Isliye libraries me 'import module' zyada safe hai.

items.q: Bare 'except Exception' catch karna kab theek hai aur kab nahi?
items.a: Theek: process/request boundary par (log + user-friendly error + continue), ya cleanup ke waqt. Nahi: business logic ke andar, jahan aap specific exception ka specific fix karna chahte ho — warna asli bug chhup jaata hai.

items.q: Exception ko log karte waqt kya zaroori hai?
items.a: Stack trace (logger.exception / exc_info=True), context (kis input par fail hua), aur correlation id — plain str(e) se trace gaya to root cause debugging aadha adhoora reh jaata hai. Sensitive values log na karo.
items.x: Trace + context, message akela kaafi nahi.

items.q: File open karte waqt encoding explicitly kyun deni chahiye?
items.a: Default platform-dependent hai, isliye same code different machine par alag behave karta hai (Windows par cp1252). encoding='utf-8' likhna reproducible behaviour deta hai aur UnicodeDecodeError se bachata hai.

items.q: Custom exception banao aur ek retry-wala function likho jo specific error par dobara try kare.
items.x: Specific exception catch karo, broad nahi.

items.q: JSON file padho aur missing/corrupt ho to safe default do.
CSV padho aur ek column ka sum nikalo (stdlib only, exceptions handled).
items.x: Row number ke saath error do — debugging aasan.

items.q: File ko atomically likho (crash ho to aadhi file na bane).
items.a:
import os, pathlib, tempfile

def write_atomic(path, text):
    p = pathlib.Path(path)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', delete=False, dir=p.parent, encoding='utf-8') as tmp:
        tmp.write(text)
        tmp.flush()
        os.fsync(tmp.fileno())
        name = tmp.name
    os.replace(name, p)

items.q: try me return hai aur finally me bhi return — kaunsa return jeetta hai?
items.a: finally wala return jeetta hai (aur woh try ka return value discard kar deta hai) — yahi reason hai ki finally me return/break likhna bug maana jaata hai, sirf cleanup karo.
items.x: finally ka return sab kuch override karta hai.

items.q: except Exception pehle aur except ValueError uske baad likha hai — ValueError catch hoga?
items.a: Nahi. ValueError Exception ka subclass hai, isliye pehla (broad) handler usse bhi le lega aur doosra code dead ho jayega. Rule: specific exceptions pehle, base class baad me.

items.q: Bare except: pass wala block Ctrl+C (KeyboardInterrupt) par kya karega?
items.a: KeyboardInterrupt ko bhi kha jaayega (kyunki bare except BaseException tak pakadta hai), isliye user ka Ctrl+C kaam nahi karega. Fix: except Exception (ya specific) use karo, aur 'pass' ki jagah log/handle karo.
items.x: Bare except KeyboardInterrupt bhi kha jaata hai.

items.q: Script ne 500 files ke baad 'Too many open files' diya. Code me kya galat hai?
items.a: File open karke close nahi kiya (with use nahi hua), isliye file descriptors leak ho rahe hain. Fix: with open(...) as f: use karo — exception par bhi handle band ho jaayega.

items.q: Production logs me sirf 'error' dikhta hai, traceback nahi. Fix?
items.a: logger.exception(...) ya logger.error(..., exc_info=True) use karo, aur error ko 'except X as e: ... raise Y(...) from e' se chain karo — bare raise ya from e ke bina original trace kho jaata hai.

items.q: UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d — kya check karoge?
items.a: File genuinely UTF-8 hai ya legacy encoding (cp1252/latin-1) — explicitly encoding='utf-8' do, aur agar source hi mixed hai to errors='replace' ke saath read karke data quality report banao. Blind ignore karne se corrupt data silently aa jaata hai.

items.q: ImportError: cannot import name 'X' from partially initialized module — classic wajah?
items.a: Circular import: A, B ko import kar raha hai aur B, A ko, aur import-time par attribute abhi bana hi nahi. Fix: import ko function ke andar le jao, shared code ko third module me nikalo, ya TYPE_CHECKING ke saath type-only import karo.
items.x: Circular import ko todna = third module.

items.q: Real-world: log file parse karo aur malformed lines ko report karke skip karo (crash na ho).
items.x: Bad count return karo — silent skip se better.

items.q: Real-world: config loader jo missing file, invalid JSON aur missing required key — teeno ko alag-alag clear error de.
Real-world: context manager likho jo operation ki duration measure kare aur slow hone par warn kare.
items.a:
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def timed(label, warn_ms=200):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
        state = 'SLOW' if ms > warn_ms else 'ok'
        print(f'{label}: {ms:.1f}ms {state}')

items.q: Checkpoint: file I/O ke teen gotchas likho.
items.a: Explicit encoding, with se close, aur naye file ke liye newline='' (CSV) — warna platform ke newline handling se data corrupt ho sakta hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare project me errors ka strategy kya hai — layer by layer batao.'
items.a: Data layer me specific exceptions (NotFound, Invalid) raise hote hain, service layer unhe domain errors me map karta hai, aur API boundary par ek handler unhe status codes + safe messages me convert karta hai (trace logs me, response me nahi).

items.q: Project defense: 'Retry kahan lagate ho aur kahan nahi?'
items.a: Sirf transient failures par (timeout, connection reset, 5xx) with bounded attempts + backoff + jitter. Validation errors, 4xx aur non-idempotent writes par nahi — warna duplicate side effects ban jaate hain.

items.q: Project defense: 'Secrets aur config kaise handle karte ho?'
items.a: Config env vars se aata hai aur startup par validate hota hai (fail fast), secrets kabhi repo me nahi jaate, logs me redact hote hain, aur example file (.env.example) placeholders ke saath version controlled hoti hai.

items.q: GIL kya hai aur usse kaunsa kaam slow hota hai?
items.a: GIL ek process me ek time par ek thread ko Python bytecode chalane deta hai, isliye CPU-bound threading se speedup nahi milta. I/O-bound threading useful hai; CPU-bound ke liye multiprocessing ya native/vectorized libraries.

items.q: Generator aur list me memory ka farq kya hai?
items.a: List saari values ek saath memory me rakhti hai; generator lazy hai (ek-ek value yield karta hai) aur state yaad rakhta hai, isliye bade/infinite sequences ke liye generator chahiye — trade-off: ek hi baar chal sakta hai.

items.q: Decorator internals me kya hota hai (syntax sugar kahan lagta hai)?
items.a: @deco function ka shortcut hai def f() ke baad f = deco(f) — deco ek callable leta hai aur naya callable return karta hai. Isliye original function wrapper ke andar band ho jaata hai aur __wrapped__/functools.wraps se metadata bachta hai.

items.q: async/await me concurrency kaise kaam karti hai (threads se alag kaise)?
items.a: Event loop single thread par coroutines ko cooperative tareeke se switch karta hai jab koi await I/O par block hota hai — koi OS thread nahi, isliye context switch sasta hai par ek blocking call poore loop ko rok deta hai. CPU-bound kaam ke liye asyncio galat tool hai.

items.q: Threads vs multiprocessing vs asyncio — interview me decision criteria batao.
items.a: I/O-bound + kai connections → asyncio; I/O-bound with blocking libraries → threads; CPU-bound (GIL wala kaam) → multiprocessing (ya C/NumPy). Aur sabse pehle measure karo ki kaam CPU-bound hai ya I/O-bound.

items.q: dataclass aur NamedTuple me kab kaunsa choose karoge?
items.a: dataclass: mutable defaults, validators, methods, inheritance — general domain models ke liye. NamedTuple: immutable tuple-like record, unpacking aur indexing chahiye — lightweight value objects ke liye.

import asyncio

async def fetch(n):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    return n * 2

async def main():
    results = await asyncio.gather(*(fetch(i) for i in range(3)))
    return results

items.q: Small ints ke liye a = 256; b = 256; a is b — True ya False, aur isse kya seekhna?
items.a: CPython me chhote ints cached hote hain, isliye True aa sakta hai (implementation detail); bade ints ya strings par False bhi ho sakta hai. Value compare karne ke liye == use karo, is ko identity ke liye.

items.q: Ek generator function ke andar return ka kya asar hota hai?
items.a: return StopIteration raise karta hai (aur return value exception ke .value me jati hai) — yani iteration wahi khatam. Isliye yield nahi hone pade to bas StopIteration milti hai aur list khaali banti hai.

items.q: Generator ko do jagah consume kiya, doosra consumer khaali result de raha hai. Fix?
items.a: Generator exhausted ho gaya — ya naya generator banao (factory function se), ya values ko list me materialize karo (memory cost), ya itertools.tee use karo (buffering ka kharcha samjho).

items.q: asyncio code chal raha hai par request ka time kam nahi hua: 'coroutine was never awaited' warning aaya. Bug?
items.a: Coroutine call kiya par await nahi kiya (ya task create nahi kiya), isliye woh kabhi execute hi nahi hui. Fix: await, ya asyncio.gather/create_task se schedule karo, aur blocking library call ko run_in_executor me bhejo.

items.q: Memory daily badh rahi hai aur restart se theek ho jaati hai. Sabse common Python wajah?
items.a: Unbounded cache/dict (ya lru_cache(maxsize=None)), listeners jo remove nahi hote, aur bade objects ko globals me hold karna. Fix: bounded caches, weakrefs/deregister, aur memory profiling (tracemalloc) se growth pakdo.

items.q: Recursive function bade input par RecursionError deta hai. Do sahi fix batao.
items.a: 1) Iterative version likho (explicit stack) — production me preferred. 2) Ya sys.setrecursionlimit badhao (par stack overflow se crash ka risk hai) plus memoization se depth kam karo. Algo redesign (DP) sabse robust hai.
